title: Three legs and a maximum-age proof
promptMarkdown: Use years and light-years. One traveller follows $A=(0,0)$, $B=(3,0)$, $C=(8,4)$, $D=(13,0)$ with straight legs. Another goes directly from A to D. Compute both elapsed proper times. Then prove the straight route gives the largest proper time for any future-directed piecewise smooth timelike route between A and D. State the equality case and why the claim is not simply a Euclidean triangle inequality.
hintLadder: Compute each segment interval before adding.
Choose the endpoint rest frame for the proof.
Analyse when the integrand equals one.
